title: Grammar-Constrained Decoding (GCD) — first-class Guardian option
purpose: Add Grammar-Constrained Decoding (GBNF / JSON-schema / response_format) as a documented, first-class option in Guardian. Primary consumer: the Keanu Factory distill pipeline, which needs strict structured JSON output from LLMs. Today the local OpenAI path passes a `grammar` field through to llama-server unmodified (body is forwarded 1:1), but this is undocumented, breaks on cloud routes, is missing on the Ollama bridge, and has no per-model toggle. Make it correct, documented, and configurable.

consumer_context.why: Distill needs guaranteed-JSON output from local models. Without GCD, distill yields invalid JSON ~5-15% of the time and depends on brittle regex parsing.
consumer_context.how_called: Keanu constructs OpenAI-format requests with `response_format: {type: "json_schema", json_schema: {...}}` (OpenAI-native structured output) OR a `grammar` GBNF string, POSTed to Guardian /v1/chat/completions.

local_openai_path.evidence: app/gateway/routing.py forwards request body 1:1 to llama-server via `content=body` on lines ~634, ~652, ~879, ~896. No field allowlist strips `grammar`/`json_schema`/`response_format`.
local_openai_path.gap: Officially unsupported — clients/passing grammar may break on a future code change that begins to normalize/whitelist body fields. Must be guaranteed by a test + explicit pass-through contract.

local_ollama_bridge.evidence: app/local_inference/ollama.py builds `openai_body` on lines ~195-203 from explicit fields (model, messages, stream, options). Ollama clients send structured output via `options.format` (a JSON schema map) but this is NOT mapped to llama-server's `grammar`/`json_schema`. The field is silently dropped.
local_ollama_bridge.fix: Map Ollama `body.options.format` → `openai_body['response_format']` (if it is a JSON-schema dict) and → `openai_body['grammar']` only if a GBNF string is supplied.

cloud_path.evidence: app/cloud_inference/forwarding.py forwards the raw body. If the client sends `grammar: "root ::= ..."`, OpenRouter/NVIDIA/OpenAI will either 400, silently ignore it, or (OpenAI) accept only their own `response_format` JSON-schema form. GBNF strings on cloud routes are never valid.
cloud_path.fix: Strip `grammar` from cloud-bound bodies. If `grammar`/`response_format` targets JSON, convert to the OpenAI-native `response_format: {type: "json_schema", json_schema: {...}}`. If non-JSON grammar + cloud model, return a clear 400 naming the provider limitation.

anthropic_bridge.evidence: Anthropic /v1/messages has no GBNF equivalent; structured output goes via `tools` (tool_use). Out of scope for this spec.

capture.evidence: app/capture/schema.py has no grammar field. Capture is policy-aware.
capture.fix: Add a `grammar_present: bool` metadata flag only (NOT the grammar itself — grammar content may encode sensitive structure). Treat the raw grammar string as `strip` by default in policy, same tier as `response_format`.

config.evidence: config/models.yaml and config/settings.yaml have no grammar-related keys.
config.fix: Add per-model `grammar_decoding` capability flag + a global toggle.

docs.fix: Document the API, the per-model toggle, and the cloud limitation.

design_principles: Local OpenAI path stays a transparent pass-through — Guardian must NOT whitelist body fields and break future llama-server fields. A regression test pins this.
Cloud routes STRIP GBNF (provider-invalid) but ACCEPT OpenAI-native response_format. Optional auto-conversion from JSON-targeting GBNF to response_format.
Config is opt-in per model. Local models default enabled; cloud models default disabled (provider semantics differ).
No new hardcoded literals (see AGENTS.md rule). All default values, toggle names, and error messages go through settings.yaml / config_loader.py.

Deployment invariant: NO restart required for docs-only changes, but a restart IS required for config_loader / models.yaml / code changes (see AGENTS.md). All code changes run through scripts/pre_restart_check.py before any restart.

supported_request_fields.name: response_format
supported_request_fields.notes: Standard OpenAI structured-output field. Pass through to llama-server on local; forward-as-is on cloud.

supported_request_fields.name: json_schema
supported_request_fields.scope: local only (llama-server accepts both schema-dict and GBNF-slotted form)
supported_request_fields.notes: llama-server accepts this field directly. Strip on cloud.

supported_request_fields.name: grammar
supported_request_fields.notes: Raw GBNF grammar string. Pass through to llama-server. Strip on cloud (unless auto-convert enabled and grammar targets JSON).

ollama_client_convention.form: either {'type':'object','properties':{...}} (JSON schema — map to response_format) or a GBNF string (map to grammar)
ollama_client_convention.notes: Map in app/local_inference/ollama.py when constructing openai_body.

implementation.title: Pin local OpenAI passthrough contract with a regression test
implementation.what: Write a test that POSTs to /v1/chat/completions on a mocked llama-server with body containing `response_format`, `json_schema`, AND `grammar` fields, and asserts the forwarded request body contains ALL THREE fields byte-identical to the input. This locks in the no-whitelist contract so a future change cannot silently break Keanu.
implementation.acceptance: Test passes on current code (proving passthrough already works) AND fails if any body-normalization step strips an unknown field (mutation-tested).

implementation.title: Fix Ollama bridge: map options.format to response_format/grammar
what: In chat_ollama (around line 194 where options = body.get('options', {})) and generate_ollama (around line 325), read options.format.
If options.format is a dict -> set openai_body['response_format'] = options.format (JSON schema path).
If options.format is a string -> set openai_body['grammar'] = options.format (GBNF path).
Do NOT shadow an explicit response_format/grammar in body if already present (client intent wins).
Add unit tests: (a) options.format dict maps to response_format, (b) options.format string maps to grammar, (c) top-level response_format is not overwritten by options.format when both present.
implementation.acceptance: An Ollama /api/chat request with options.format reaches llama-server with response_format set; new tests pass.

implementation.title: Cloud grammar stripping + JSON-schema auto-conversion in forwarding
what: Before forwarding the body to a cloud provider, call a new helper _strip_cloud_grammar(body, *, allow_json_convert) that returns a new body dict.

If body has `grammar` (GBNF string): pop it. If allow_json_convert is true AND the cfg.enabled setting grammar.cloud_auto_convert_json is true AND the GPU grammar parses as JSON-proxyable, emit body['response_format'] = {type: 'json_schema', json_schema: <derived>}. Otherwise drop the field and log a warning (do NOT 500 unless strict_mode).
If body has `json_schema` (non-OpenAI-native form): pop it and (if allow_json_convert) convert to response_format.
response_format (OpenAI-native) is preserved as-is on cloud.
New config setting (settings.yaml): grammar.cloud_auto_convert_json: false (default) and grammar.cloud_strict_mode: false (default).

Add unit tests: (1) grammar stripped from cloud body, (2) response_format preserved on cloud, (3) when cloud_auto_convert_json is true a JSON GBNF becomes response_format, (4) in strict_mode=true an unsupported grammar on a cloud model returns HTTP 400 with an error naming the provider.
implementation.acceptance: POST /v1/chat/completions with body.grammar to a guardian/openrouter/... model no longer forwards the GBNF string; tests pass.

implementation.title: Per-model capability flag in models.yaml + config_loader accessor
what: Add optional per-model key in models.yaml: `grammar_decoding: true|false` (defaults: true for local, false for cloud routes). This is a hint for the dashboard / docs and gates the GraMMAR STripping behavior is gated by this + global grammar.enabled.

Add global toggle in settings.yaml: `grammar.enabled: true` (default), `grammar.cloud_auto_convert_json: false` (default), `grammar.cloud_strict_mode: false` (default), `grammar.validate_gbnf: false` (default — GBNF parsing is optional).
Add typed accessors in config_loader.py: get_grammar_enabled(), get_grammar_cloud_auto_convert_json(), get_grammar_cloud_strict_mode(), get_grammar_validate_gbnf().
When grammar.enabled is false at the process level, ALL grammars are stripped on BOTH local and cloud paths (kill-switch for emergency response).
implementation.acceptance: config_loader returns new fields with defaults when unset; existing tests still pass.

implementation.title: Optional GBNF pre-validation in normalization
what: When config.grammar.validate_gbnf is true, attempt to parse the `grammar` field's GBNF. On parse error, raise HTTPException(400) with a clear message: 'Invalid GBNF grammar: <detail>'.
Do NOT validate when flag is false (default) — defer to llama-server's parser.
If no GBNF parser is importable, skip silently and log (fail-open).
tests: (1) valid GBNF passes through unchanged, (2) invalid GBNF returns 400 with detail only when flag is true, (3) no-op when flag false.
implementation.acceptance: Erroneous grammars return a clean 400 instead of a raw llama-server error.

implementation.title: Capture grammar_present flag (no grammar content)
what: Add metadata field `grammar_present: bool` and `response_format_present: bool` to the capture event schema (NO raw grammar or schema content — treated as sensitive structure).
Default policy: grammar content is `strip` (same tier as response_format).
In capture_dispatch (request_received path), set grammar_present = 'grammar' in json_body or 'response_format' in json_body or 'json_schema' in json_body.
tests: events reflect the boolean without leaking content.
implementation.acceptance: Capture events expose the flag; secrets/canaries tests still pass.

implementation.title: Documentation
what: docs/API_REFERENCE.md: new section 'Grammar-Constrained Decoding' (see content_template below).
docs/LLM_ROUTER.md: note that cloud routes strip GBNF and (optionally) auto-convert JSON grammars to response_format, citing the config keys.
AGENTS.md: add a Critical rule summary in the Skills/index and an entry to the Active Handoff describing the feature, the FEAT ids implemented, and the config keys.
content_template: Guardian supports three structured-output fields, mapped to llama-server on the local path and to OpenAI-provider conventions on cloud routes.
| json_schema | dict / GBNF schema | pass-through | stripped, optional JSON conversion |
| grammar | string (GBNF) | pass-through | stripped, optional JSON conversion |
Ollama clients send `options.format`. Guardian maps a dict value to `response_format` and a string value to `grammar` before forwarding to llama-server.
- settings.yaml: grammar.enabled (default true), grammar.cloud_auto_convert_json (default false), grammar.cloud_strict_mode (default false), grammar.validate_gbnf (default false).

Cloud providers (OpenRouter, NVIDIA, OpenAI, Google) do NOT accept GBNF grammar strings. By default they are stripped silently. Enable grammar.cloud_auto_convert_json:true to auto-convert a JSON-targeting grammar to a response_format JSON-schema; enable grammar.cloud_strict_mode:true to return 400 instead of stripping for non-JSON grammars on cloud models.
implementation.acceptance: Docs readable, examples validate against actual Guardian behavior (test pairs exist).

verification_protocol: py_compile all touched files: ./venv/bin/python -m py_compile app/**/*py
Run pre-restart gate: ./venv/bin/python scripts/pre_restart_check.py — all 4 gates MUST pass before any restart.
Full unit suite: ./venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/ -x — no regressions (current baseline 893+ passed).
New FEAT tests pass individually: pytest tests/unit/test_grammar_passthrough.py tests/unit/test_grammar_cloud_stripping.py tests/unit/test_ollama_grammar_mapping.py
Manual smoke (after operator restarts Guardian with operator present per Critical rule): curl /v1/chat/completions with response_format JSON-schema to a local model — output parses as valid JSON.
Manual smoke: same request to a guardian/openrouter/<cloud> model — response_format preserved, grammar (if any) stripped, no 400 unless strict_mode enabled.
Inspect capture event includes grammar_present:true and does NOT include grammar string.

critical_rules_compliance.no_hardcoded_vars: All default values, toggle names, and error strings come from settings.yaml or config_loader accessors — no literals in domain logic. (AGENTS.md rule)
critical_rules_compliance.agents_md_update: AGENTS.md Active Handoff MUST be updated in the same session as the implementation (AGENTS.md rule).
critical_rules_compliance.restart_safety: Code changes require a Guardian restart which drops the agent's own session. Implement, run pre_restart_check.py, then ask the operator to restart — DO NOT restart from inside the session. (AGENTS.md Critical rule)
critical_rules_compliance.pre_restart_gate: Run scripts/pre_restart_check.py before every restart. All 4 gates (py_compile + pyflakes + signature check + pytest) MUST pass.
critical_rules_compliance.secrets: No API keys in tests or docs. All mock bodies use fake values.
critical_rules_compliance.config_loader_pattern: YAML is parsed ONCE per process (config_loader.py). Add accessors there — do not re-parse settings.yaml in domain modules.

acceptance_summary: GCD is a first-class, documented option: (1) local OpenAI passthrough is guaranteed by a regression test, (2) Ollama bridge maps options.format correctly, (3) cloud routes strip GBNF and optionally auto-convert JSON grammars, (4) per-model + global config toggles exist, (5) capture exposes only a presence flag, (6) docs explain the API and caveats, (7) all gates pass before restart.
out_of_scope: Anthropic /v/messages structured output via tools (Anthropic has no GBNF).
GBNF authoring tooling or a grammar library — Guardian is a proxy, not an authoring surface.
Cloud GBNF execution (impossible by provider design).
Changing the local queue behavior — GCD does not affect scheduling.
report_back: Provide: FEAT id list with status (implemented/skipped), files changed, diff highlights for the passthrough test + cloud stripping + Ollama mapping, pytest output counts, pre_restart_check.py result, and the exact config keys added.
